newsitem.title: USA: Collagen resumes shipments of Contigen.
newsitem.headline: Collagen resumes shipments of Contigen.

text.p: Collagen Corp said Monday it resumed shipping its Contigen implant product.
The company said in a statement it received orders from C.R. Bard, marketer of Contigen implants to be shipped during the current quarter ending June 30.
The orders are the first in almost two years since Collagen stopped shipping Contigen to C.R. Bard to help Bard work down its excess inventories.

"We are optimistic that future shipments of Contigen implants will track in line with end-market demand for the product, which has been in the range of $35 million to $36 million per year," said President and Chief Executive Gary Petersmeyer.
"If this happens, Collagen's revenues from Contigen implant could rise from about $8 million in fiscal 1997 to about $15 million in fiscal 1998," he said.
Contigen implant is an injectable collagen product for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence caused by intrinsic sphincter deficiency.
